page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-96 is an instance belonging to the Network Optimized family, architected for compute-heavy workloads requiring substantial processing scale. It provides 96 dedicated vCPUs built on x86_64 processor architecture, alongside 192.0 GB of system memory. The resource ratio is calibrated at 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, reflecting a compute-focused distribution suitable for parallel calculations where per-thread CPU throughput takes priority over expansive memory capacity.

Hardware provisions on this instance do not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, with GPU allocation fixed at zero. Persistent file systems and high-throughput data volumes must be provisioned externally through network-attached block storage. The lack of built-in local NVMe drives requires deployments to rely on network input/output pipelines, aligning with its placement in the Network Optimized classification.

Qualitatively, the c4n-highcpu-96 delivers high CPU core density within a single node, maximizing compute throughput while avoiding the cost overhead of unutilized memory or idle accelerator silicon. Potential operational tradeoffs center on the dependency on external block storage and zero bundled IPv4 addresses. This instance profile is structurally aligned with distributed compute jobs, continuous integration and build pipelines, CPU-bound scientific simulations, and scalable web backend clusters.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-96 is a network-optimized server instance engineered for compute-centric workloads requiring high core density. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 96 dedicated vCPUs matched with 192.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance includes no GPU accelerators and provides no onboard local disk storage, necessitating network-attached storage solutions for all operating system and application persistent data. By dedicating hardware resources primarily toward raw CPU execution without the financial overhead of large memory pools or specialized GPU silicon, it maintains strong resource efficiency for processor-saturated tasks. The c4n-highcpu-96 is well matched for compute-bound network applications, distributed compile jobs, large-scale batch processing, and CPU-intensive parallel processing tasks.
